source_review.notes: Checked RFC 9110 request-content and 413/415/422 semantics; official JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 Core and Validation vocabularies; the current OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet; Unicode 17.0 UAX #15 revision 57 and its compatibility-normalization warning; and RFC 9457 Problem Details.

evidence: Reviewed the layered admission conjunction, normalization function, transformation chain, admitted-language set, and each L/P/S/n/D/T/Z definition against the prose.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All symbols are introduced, the state/context dependencies are consistent, and automated GitHub-math diagnostics report no issue.

evidence: Executed six staged fixtures: one normalized acceptance and five expected rejections for type, range, unknown field, unsupported SKU, and insufficient current stock.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The accepted ABC-1 quantity and all six output classifications match the declared expectation.

evidence: Checked that normalization either precedes effective-value validation or requires preservation, and that structural, stable-domain, mutable-state, and authorization predicates remain independent necessary obligations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The admitted-language notation is explicitly not an atomicity proof and does not collapse parser or execution semantics.

evidence: Reviewed compression expansion, nesting, duplicate names, huge digits, regex cost, Unicode normalization and confusables, decimal limits, timestamp relations, uniqueness races, hidden references, file parsers, SSRF redirects and DNS, batches, asynchronous late failure, and error amplification.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Resource, parser, structure, normalization, domain, state, authority, interpreter, and diagnostic boundaries are each covered.

evidence: Checked bounded work, one interpretation, effective-value preservation, full-object consistency, authorized lookup, atomic state enforcement, safe interpreters, non-disclosing errors, and reproducible configuration across examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: No section claims validation replaces authorization, parameterization, object authorization, or commit-time constraints.

proof_review.notes: No formal theorem or universal admission proof is claimed.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; the pipeline equations are specification and review models.

evidence: The executable fixture explicitly disclaims HTTP parsing, authorization, races, and production conformance; recommended replay and telemetry are described as bounded rollout evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: OWASP guidance is used normatively for engineering cautions rather than as measured prevalence evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the end-to-end pipeline from framed bytes through parsing, structure, normalization, domain and state predicates, authority, safe execution, diagnostics, and compatibility.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed status taxonomy, parser configuration, exact numbers, Unicode, regex, unknown fields, PATCH results, database constraints, concealment, uploads, URLs, batches, async admission, and change rollout.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed first-principles stage inventory, executable six-case fixture, ten distinct boundary examples, and five exercises progressing from payment admission through Unicode, outcome classification, hostile imports, and constraint evolution.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
